reviews.comment: Nope...I'm outta here. Enjoy the rest of train ride folks.
Please save yourself, do not take this man.

Avoid karsilayan for ECEN 325. He teaches like everyone already has a PhD and skips massive algebraic steps. His slides are a nightmare of mixed equation formats and convoluted math with zero explanation. Prepare to spend hours reverse-engineering his slide vomit just to learn. Be ready to teach yourself everything.

There is zero mercy when it comes to Karsilayan. If you ask him questions, he rarely gives a clear answer especially when it comes to what will be on the exam. He blatantly lied and said diodes would be on the final but they were not. He even laughed at me during office hours for a question I asked. The fact I even passed is beyond me.

The WOAT. Incapable of teaching. "The slides look like a schizophrenic's rambling" is the best I've heard it put. If possible, I recommend delaying taking this class if Aydin is your only choice. If you have to, just self study and tune him out during mandatory lectures. Also, become best friends with the TA. May God have mercy on your soul.

Not fun. My advice: just use AI to be your lecturer. The lectures make no sense, as his handwriting is from a child, and he just rambles over the slides. The labs take forever, and he doesn't make it any easier by disallowing open access labs. I got a 23 and a 35 on the midterms, struggled on the final, and somehow make a B. Stick it out.

Here is an honest and fair review: Lectures are humorous and very informative. No surprises on the exams. all questions will be lab/homework content. The Lab portion is a legit 40 hour per week job (I'm dead serious). He will never instruct how to do the homework, you just have to be an expert in ECEN326 already.

One attempt homeworks that were more difficult than other profs. Made our lab harder by not letting us prebuild circuits. Made exams extremely difficult. Easily the toughest ECEN class, at least with Aydin. You do get to complain about him to people that have Oscar, so that's nice. Needed a very heavy curve to pass, thinking Im getting C maybe B.
he eats too much chicken
I dont know why he loves shawarma so much but he uses rotating shawarma spit as an analogy for nyquist plot. The out there analogies make it easy to lose the plot of the lecture..
One time I caught him sleeping on the job.

ECEN 704 - The class is in no way 4 credits. It is worth at least 9 credits with labs. Each lab takes a week to do. And you don't receive most of your lab grades until last week of semester, so you don't know what you did wrong or right. His canvas hw answers are wrong sometimes and he doesn't give any partial credit.

Dr. Karsilayan emphasizes what you need to know and prioritizes efficiency when solving problems. All practice problems are previous exam problems and he gives the solutions.  If you ask by email or during OH, he gives thorough explanations about components and concepts. He heavily curves (mid 40s was an A on exam 1) which is nice.

I dropped this class with another prof(was a mistake I prob would have passed) and took it with this prof. 10x harder test and HW problems that are basically impossible. Both midterms I got in the 20s and studied my a** off. HWs are one attempt and you don't get solutions. Basically impossible to learn. Somehow got a C idk what the curve was.
Me watching LVS fail at 3:37AM :DDDDD
Worst class ever taken.Avoid it at any cost
Goofy ahh professor

Lectures aren't very helpful but the slides are good. Homework and grading policies are much tougher than other professors for seemingly no reason. Grading is opaque; assignments turned in in late February weren't graded until finals week. Exam class averages hover in the low 20s, course gets curved heavily to compensate.

No exceptions.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best instructors at TAMU. The amount of content I learned from him amazes me. It's important to pay attention to lectures as he gives great hints or industry advice. Get really fast at the homework problems and you'll place well above the (really low) test averages. Labs take a long time to do. Its a trial by fire, but he cares.

reviews.comment: Homework will help, but make sure to do reviews. He is difficult to understand and not clear on explaining some topics. I read and did examples in the book and still was confused. The final is extremely difficult. Make sure to study and do reviews and extra practice.

reviews.comment: Karsilayan is tough but extremely knowledgeable about the material. His lectures are very dense, and it can be easy to fall behind or get lost. His notes are good for that most part but sometimes difficult to follow by themselves. Karsilayan is often extremely passive aggressive and can be difficult to approach with questions. Averages are low.
Has little concern for teaching or helping out students even if you ask for help. Avoid him unless you already know the subject and can practically teach it to someone.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult but well worth the pain. Lectures clearly teach concepts and prof emphasizes the importance of intuitively understanding amplifier structures. Will absolutely take again for 704.

I didn't find him very helpful or kind when asking questions. I would recommend any of the other 325 professors if you want to be able to learn useful content in class without having to feel ashamed of needing help.

Dr. Karsilayan refuses to simplify any concepts to aid in understanding during lecture, his lecture slides are undecipherable unless you rewatch entire lectures, and you receive NO feedback on any assignment or exam. His courses are harder than any other professor for no reason other than him, take anyone else available.

reviews.comment: This professor goes out of the way to help students understand concepts.

The exams are hard, but if you take advantage of the resources he gives you, you'll do fine. Dr. Karsilayan is incredibly knowledgeable and presents the material well. Most people complaining about this class don't go to lecture, do the homework, or study. Trust me, if you reasonably participate, you'll do well.

Dr. Karsilayan is incredibly knowledgeable on the subject matter and presents it in a way such that I know it very well going forward. He's definitely tough, but most of the people who complain about him also don't go to class, do the homework, or take advantage of any of the resources he gives to students.

My main problem with this professor is he tries to convey too much information. He understands the material so well its hard for him to understand why other people dont get it. He just refuses to simplify anything, introductions go to complicated examples in a snap and everything is graded so hard that he has to curve. Youll most likely pass though
Labs can be a lot of work. Homework problems are all or nothing, no partial credit. If you know circuits better than Dr. Karsilayan, youll probably pass the class.

reviews.comment: They say to avoid Oscar Moreira-Tamayo "at all costs" but let me tell you, this is the one cost you do not want to pay to avoid him. Dr. K is the hardest professor I've ever had. His exams are impossible to do unless you're Einstein. He is very brash and his teaching is just awful. If it's Tamayo vs Karsilayan, choose Tamayo. Lesser of two evils.

Each quiz had about on question on it. His grading was merciless. You either got a 100% or <30%. If you ended up with the correct answer but messed up in the work,then you lost points

Dr. Karsilayan is truly the toughest professor in the ECEN department. On top of that, he requires that you understand the material as well as he does if you want to do well, which is impossible. reviews.comment: I've had 3 courses(325,326,474) with Dr. Karsilayan and can verify that he is among the toughest profs at TAMU. That being said he is easily the best prof in the ECEN department. All his assignments have purpose, with a heavy emphasis on intuition over math. If you want a genuine understanding of transistors, this is your guy!

This prof is there to fail his students. You pass by chance, the exam averages are very low. If it weren't for my TA, I would have failed. The TA teaches this class 100x better, which is an indication of just how bad this prof is. The TA was his grad student, and even she left him for a better advisor. Any other prof is better, Palermo is best.

ECEN325 is a ridiculous class regardless of the prof you have. Dr. Karsilayan makes it even worse bc of the insane amount of hw. This class can take 10-20 hours a week.
